## "It's not the outskirts killing me, it's the city. And the people who run the city have names and addresses."

The exile is a ronin who has found themselves afoul of the city, pushed away by some merit of the people, the power, or their personal need. The outskirts become their defacto home, insofar as the dangers beyond the city limits are any one individual's home. The nature of the exile will push them away from the safety that pockmarks the desert, the rainforest, and the bunker homes, instead crashing against the death that lurks in the dunes, trees, and forgotten terminals. Should they survive, their return to the city will know them deathless.

##### Source: Unearthed Arcana (Brute), Neon City NightsThis is a reny joint, with the Mechanics team providing adjustments and suggestions!

### No Rest For The Wicked

Beginning when you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you become immune to physical exhaustion, or fatigue, as the result of your own actions, such as long periods of travel or extended periods of physical strain and activity. Fatigue caused by specific features, abilities, or effects still applies.

In addition, while you are at half your hit points or less, a state referred to as bloodied, whenever you hit with an attack and deal damage, the damage increases by 1d4.

### Can't Slow Down

Also at 3rd level, you've learned that the only true path of survival is one of constant motion, and so refuse to rest or let your injuries slow your assault. You gain two additional uses of your second wind feature. When you use a bonus action to regain hit points using your second wind feature, you can also choose to expend a number of hit dice up to your proficiency Bonus to gain a number of temporary hit points equal to the number rolled + your Constitution modifier, and you can make one weapon attack as part of the same bonus action. Starting at 7th level, this attack is made at advantage.

### Can't Hold Back

Starting at 7th level, you gain resistance to entropic and poison damage, and you have advantage on saving throws against disease and exhaustion. Your grim disposition puts off even the approach of death, you add half of your Intimidation modifier to your death saving throws. Once per long rest, if applying this bonus increases the total to a 20 or higher, you gain the benefits of rolling a 20 on the d20.

Additionally, the promise of your ire allows you just a moment's more breathing room. When you would be granted an attack thanks to can't slow down, you can forfeit the attack and regain hit points equal to your Intimidation modifier for each attack forfeited.

### Cracked Reactions

At 10th level, you conserve your energy where you can, a corpse like stillness giving way to frenzied retaliation when least expected, allowing you to recoup on another man's time. You gain two additional uses of your second wind feature, for a total of four additional uses. When you are hit with an attack, you can use your reaction to tank the blow, immediately using your second wind, making an attack with the same reaction as per can't slow down. If the triggering attack does not deplete the temporary hit points gained from can't slow down, you can make an additional attack as part of the same reaction, and move up to half your movement, without triggering opportunity attacks, before doing so.

In addition, while you are at one fourth your hit points or less, a state referred to as critical, whenever you hit with an attack and deal damage, the damage increases by 1d8, instead of 1d4.

### Until We Close Our Eyes

Starting at 15th level, you are immune to disease, exhaustion from non-technical sources, and you have advantage on saving throws against the poisoned, unconscious, and incapacitated conditions. Whenever you roll initiative or return to 1 hit point as a result of rolling a 20 on a death save, you can expend and roll one hit die, gaining an amount of hit points equal to the roll + your Constitution modifier.

### Die On Your Feet

At 18th level, your hardships have allowed you to thoroughly straddle the border between life and death and call it your bitch. You gain two additional uses of your second wind feature, for a total of six additional uses. You do not lose consciousness or become incapacitated while at 0 hit points, and taking damage while you are at 0 hit points does not impose any failed death saves. You can not take actions, reactions, or move while in this state, except for taking a bonus action to automatically fail one death save, which then allows you to take the rest of your turn as normal.

In addition, while you are at 0 hit points, whenever you hit with an attack and deal damage, the damage increases by 1d12, instead of 1d8.
